newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-INDIA GRIND OUT THE RUNS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-INDIA GRIND OUT THE RUNS.

text.p: India crawled to 41 for one by lunch after winning the toss on the opening day of the third and final test against South Africa on Thursday.

After scoring just 25 runs in 22 overs the opening stand was broken by the first ball from wrist spinner Paul Adams. Adams had recalled opener Vikram Rathore caught behind for 13 runs chiselled out from 69 balls.
The new ball pair of Allan Donald and Shaun Pollock caused relatively few problems for Rathore and Nayan Mongia on an overcast morning.
The first chance came in the 22nd over when paceman Lance Klusener found the edge of Rathore's bat only to see first slip Daryll Cullinan miss a simple catch.
But Rathore added only a single to his total before falling to the wiles of Adams.
The 27-year-old from the Punjab was the only change to the Indian side which lost the second test in Cape Town. South Africa were unchanged.
